in_text_mentions: Six of 31 examined patients had extensive composite dental restorations, most probably secondary to underlying enamel defects. Another 18 (72%) had enamel hypoplasia typical for APS1 (Figure 2), and five had enamel hypomineralization without enamel hypoplasia, which could be of different etiology. The enamel hypoplasia varied in extent and location. Nine patients had gingivitis, and eight patients presented pathologically low (below 0.1 mL/min) unstimulated salivary flow.

panels.figure_caption: In vivo confocal microscopy findings of the cornea. a, b Squamous epithelial layer. White arrows indicate the elongated squamous epithelial cells with a tendency to slough off. c, d White arrows indicate the sub-basal nerve plexus, which was either tortuous and beading in the right eye (c), or short and fragmented in the left eye (d). The density of the nerve plexus was also severely affected. e, f White arrows indicate the corneal nerve bundle in the anterior stromal layer. Both eyes showed a significant decrease in the width, density, and length of the anterior corneal stromal nerve bundles compared with normal eyes

In both eyes, the stromal nerve bundles became very thin and torturous (Fig. 3e, f), which is quite different from the thick stromal nerve bundles in normal corneas. in_text_mentions: e of the fever, with a typical electroencephalogram aspect. The patient underwent a cerebral computed tomography scan to investigate the causes of these recurrent seizures, which revealed diffuse basal ganglia and frontal cortex calcifications without evidence of infarction, hemorrhage, or mass effect (Figure 1). Despite receiving optimal doses of anticonvulsant drugs (valproic acid and levetiracetam), the patient remained unresponsive to treatment, presenting several daily seizure episodes lasting no longer than two minutes, often recovering spontaneously without any therapeutic intervention.

plate_findings.evidence: caption: 'Superficial esophageal mucosa ((a),(b)) invaded by candidal psudohyphae'; in-text: 'upper GI Endoscopy ... revealed candida esophagitis'

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 7 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F, G). A: Grocott-silver histology of esophageal mucosa from an APECED patient showing invasive candidal pseudohyphae; chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis is a hallmark APECED manifestation, and the disease-focused title plus the specific captioned manifestation support attribution. B: Higher-magnification Grocott-silver histology of the same esophageal candidiasis in an APECED patient; candidiasis is a core APECED manifestation and the article title plus captioned finding support attribution. C: PAS-stained renal biopsy glomerulus from the APECED case; the article title frames the renal failure as APECED-associated autoimmune nephropathy, so the biopsy is attributed to the target disease, though no vocabulary finding key matches this glomerular lesion. D: Masson trichrome renal biopsy showing chronic tubular injury and fibrosis; attributed to APECED-associated autoimmune nephropathy per the disease-focused title and in-text description...
panels.attribution_text: Al-Owain et al. Renal failure associated with APECED and terminal 4q deletion: evidence of autoimmune nephropathy.. Clinical & developmental immunology 2010. doi:10.1155/2010/586342. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Superficial esophageal mucosa ((a),(b)) invaded by candidal psudohyphae. Grocott-Methenamine silver (original magnification 200x (a)/400x (b)). Renal biopsy ((c), (d), (e)) shows ischemic glomerular tuft with thick and wrinkled basement membrane (PAS stain 40x) (c) and extensive tubular loss with replacement by fibrosis (Masson trichrome stain 40x) (d). The interstitium shows lymphocytes and plasma cells (arrows) (H&E 40x) (e). The immunofluorescence staining for C3 and C1q is shown in (f) and (g), respectively.
in_text_mentions: ve a robust response to mitogens and other antigens. He was treated with oral fluconazole. Because of recurrent vomiting, an upper GI Endoscopy was performed and revealed candida esophagitis (Figures 2(a) and 2(b)). The presence of diffuse cerebellar atrophy was noted on followup MRI. Developmentally, the patient had global delays. He sat at 1 year and stood with support at 2 years. Bayley Scales of Infant Development when the patient was 2.5 years old revealed a mental age of 11 months and a motor age of 6 months. Review of the family history was negative for recognized genetic conditions, co

The renal biopsy (Figures 2(c), 2(d), and 2(e)) showed chronic tubular interstitial nephritis with advanced fibrosis. The immunofluorescence demonstrated mesangial deposition of C3 (3+), C1q (2+) (Figures 2(f) and 2(g)), and IgM (1+) (figure not shown) in the glomerulus examined. The remaining immunoglobulins were negative in the glomerular basement membrane, mesangium, and extraglomerular structures.
